s1.syndrome_frame: Rapidly progressive gait disturbance with spinal cord compression
salient_findings: Decreased sensation from the T3 dermatome downward
Clonus and hyperreflexia in the lower extremities
Diffusely enhancing lesion centered at T1 with near-circumferential epidural extension on MRI
key_facts: 1-week history of rapidly progressive gait disturbance
No back pain, fevers, night sweats, or weight loss
No history of smoking or known malignancy
Full strength throughout all extremities
Decreased sensation from the T3 dermatome downward
Four beats of clonus bilaterally
Hyperreflexia in the lower extremities
Profound ataxia
Expansile bony lesion of the T1 vertebral body with extension into the left pedicle and posterior elements on CT
No evidence of primary malignancy on CT scans of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis
Laboratory studies, including inflammatory markers, were within normal limits

shortlist.label: Chordoma
shortlist.why_kept: Expansile bony lesion of the T1 vertebral body with extension into the left pedicle and posterior elements on CT

shortlist.label: Plasmacytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rapidly progressive neurological decline with spinal cord compression and no evidence of primary malignancy

shortlist.label: Multiple myeloma
shortlist.why_kept: Rapidly progressive neurological decline with spinal cord compression and no evidence of primary malignancy

shortlist.label: Metastatic lung cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Rapidly progressive neurological decline with spinal cord compression, although no primary malignancy was found on CT scans

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rapidly progressive neurological decline with spinal cord compression and no evidence of primary malignancy

raw.rationale: The expansile bony lesion of the T1 vertebral body with extension into the left pedicle and posterior elements, along with the absence of primary malignancy and normal laboratory studies, is most consistent with a chordoma, which is a rare, slow-growing bone tumor that can cause neurological symptoms due to spinal cord compression.

rejected.label: Plasmacytoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with back pain and elevated inflammatory markers, which are not present in this case

rejected.label: Multiple myeloma
rejected.why: Usually associated with systemic symptoms such as weight loss, night sweats, and elevated inflammatory markers, which are not present in this case

rejected.label: Metastatic lung cancer
rejected.why: Patient has no history of smoking or known malignancy, and CT scans of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis revealed no evidence of primary malignancy

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with systemic symptoms such as weight loss, night sweats, and fever, which are not present in this case
